generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from the parent table's generated PK values; allow NULL only when the column is nullable; include parent rows without children by leaving some parent PKs unreferenced.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity: Positive integers in a plausible range (1..1000) unless a per-column exception narrows it.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_count: Non-negative integers in 0..5000; include NULL only for nullable columns.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Title-cased or mixed-case short names built from a fixed vocabulary; length within declared limit; 5% near-variant duplicates (case change, trailing char, one-char substitution).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_nullable: 80% non-NULL values, 20% NULL; never NULL on NOT NULL columns.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numeric: For each listed literal L, emit L-1, L, L+1.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_text: For each listed literal L, emit exact L, lower(L), upper(L), and one near-variant (append 'x', drop last char, or one-char substitution).
generic_sampling_rules.like_variant: For each LIKE literal, emit the base token, a one-char typo variant, an upper-case variant, and a variant with an extra trailing char.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_share: On DISTINCT-target columns, 20-50% of rows repeat an earlier value.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_rank: On ORDER/LIMIT target columns, plant at least two rows sharing the boundary value.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, at least one NULL row per instance; share ~20% unless a per-column exception states otherwise.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_values: All non-key text values are freshly generated from the vocabulary; no copying from original rows.

targets.rule: Leave 10-20% of parent PKs unreferenced by any child row; nullable FKs (paper.venueId, paper.journalId) also get NULL rows.
NOT NULL columns never NULL; nullable count-like columns (paper.numCiting, paper.numCitedBy) get ~20% NULL.
Plant at least two rows sharing the boundary value at each listed LIMIT rank.

issues.evidence: Specification's per_column_exceptions for comparison_boundary lists paper.paperId values [1057,1058,1059] and writes.paperId values [-1,0,1,2009,2010,2011], but the atomic summary shows these are boundary values for PRED(writes.paperid >= paper.paperid) — a join predicate, not a constant comparison. The spec's boundary_numeric rule ('emit L-1, L, L+1') is applied to these as if they were literal constants, which is a reasonable interpretation but not strictly what the atomic op describes.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the spec that join-predicate boundary values are planted as literal values on the respective columns (as the program does), or drop them from boundary_numeric if they are not intended as constant-comparison boundaries.

issues.evidence: Specification's semantic_rules_and_formulas include 'writes.paperId > 0' and 'writes.authorId > 0', but the boundary_numeric exception for writes.paperId lists values [-1, 0, 1, ...] and writes.authorId lists [0, 1, 2]. These are contradictory: planting -1/0 on writes.paperId violates the stated 'paperId > 0' rule. The program's _apply_semantic_rules does not enforce writes.paperId > 0 (only cite self-exclusion and paper ranges), so the planted -1/0 survive. Execution feedback shows 0 integrity violations because the DB has no CHECK on writes.paperId, but the spec's own formula is violated by its own boundary rule.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the spec: either remove 'writes.paperId > 0' / 'writes.authorId > 0' from semantic_rules_and_formulas (since boundary values include 0 and -1), or remove 0/-1 from the boundary values. The program should then enforce whichever is chosen.

issues.evidence: instance.py _apply_semantic_rules does not enforce the spec's 'writes.paperId > 0' and 'writes.authorId > 0' formulas. Boundary planting of -1/0 on writes.paperId (BOUNDARY_NUMERIC) is applied after FK fill and is not corrected. This is consistent with the boundary exception but inconsistent with the semantic formula in the spec.
issues.requested_revision: Once the designer reconciles the contradiction, ensure the program enforces the final rule (e.g., skip planting 0/-1 on writes.paperId if the >0 rule stands, or drop the >0 rule).

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_boundary_numeric for ('paper','paperId') plants 1057,1058,1059 (and L-1/L+1) directly into paper.paperId, overwriting the sequential fresh PKs assigned by _fresh_pk_values. This can create PK collisions with other planted values or with the sequential range, and can break the 'sequential integers starting at 1' rule. Execution feedback shows 0 pk_duplicates across 20 instances, so in practice the overwrite did not collide, but the ordering (fresh PKs then boundary plant) is fragile.
issues.requested_revision: Plant boundary values on paper.paperId before or instead of the sequential assignment, or verify no collision after planting (the program's sample_fresh_primary_keys runs before planting, so a post-plant dedup is missing).

issues.evidence: instance.py _apply_unmatched_join runs after all planting and rewrites FK values to a random kept subset, which can overwrite planted boundary FK values (e.g., paper.venueId boundary 2014/2015/2016, paperKeyphrase.paperId boundary 0..3). The boundary planting for paper.venueId and paperKeyphrase.paperId may be partially undone. Execution feedback does not report boundary-value presence, so this is unverified.
issues.requested_revision: Apply unmatched_join before boundary planting, or exclude boundary-planted rows from the unmatched-join rewrite, so boundary values survive.
